reader.requirement: At --std 85 FUNCTION MAX returns the content of the argument-1 with the greatest value, comparing as simple conditions do: numeric arguments by algebraic value regardless of scale and length, alphabetic/alphanumeric arguments (groups and edited items included) character by character in the program collating sequence with the shorter extended by spaces; arguments may be a table with ALL subscripts over an ODO table.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 window sig.IntroducedIn (85): MAX admitted at 85
ArgPredicate.AppliesAt(year): per-edition argument predicates (class mixing); the selection itself is unaffected

reader.edition-search: grep of IntrinsicCarrierRules.cs, FunctionValueLane.cs, IntrinsicRenderer.cs, CobolIntrinsics.Select.cs/Exact.cs/Dec.cs for Edition, DialectLevel, DialectBehavior, ConstructRegistry: no hit on the selection path; the collating sequence reaches MaxString through the program's PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, not an edition switch.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf40_01 covers mixed-scale and signed numerics and two alphanumeric shapes in native order; it does not cover a program collating sequence, a group or edited argument, ALL over an ODO table, 18-digit values, negative fractions, or an argument that is also the receiver.

probes.expected: ALL over the current 3 occurrences -> 4.5, over 4 -> 9; S9(18) 999999999999999999 beats ...998 (shown low-order-truncated in a 9(15).9(3) receiver); MAX(-0.1 -0.01 -1) = -0.01; MAX(0 -0) = 0; COMPUTE K = MAX(K 3) + K with K 7 = 14
under PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE REV ("Z" "Y" "B" "A") 'A' is greatest: MAX("A" "Z") = A, MAX("AB" "BA" "YA") = AB, MAX(group "AB", "B") = AB; edited " 12.50" vs "100.00" -> 100.00

probes.printed: COBOL0900 numeric-literal VALUE for a numeric-edited item requires COBOL-2023; COBOL0802 19 digit positions, COBOL-85 limits to 18

reader.notes: Numeric MAX selects on exact scaled values (MaxAt/MaxDec) and returns the selected argument's value; alphanumeric MAX selects through CobolString.Compare or the program's collation (MaxString with the collation overload), space-extending the shorter operand. The probes under a reversed alphabet confirm the program collating sequence decides the comparison, as the simple-condition rules require.

refuter.evidence: Attack on the space-extension half of the simple-condition comparison under a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE (ALPHABET REV IS "Z" "Y" "B" "A": space, unlisted, follows every listed letter). Probe rmx1.cob at --std 85 (runs/rmx1-001): MAX("A" "AB") -> 'A', MAX("AB" "A") -> 'A', MAX(X2 'AB', A1 'A') -> 'A' ("A " compares greater than "AB" because space ranks above B), LENGTH of the result 1; numeric-edited ZZ9.99CR ' 12.50CR' against '  12.50' -> ' 12.50CR' (space below '1' in native order of unlisted characters); two-dimension table C(ALL, ALL) -> 7, C(1, ALL) -> 5, C(ALL, 3) -> 6.
